entries.label: Ethernet Virtual Connection (EVC)
entries.definition: The customer's carrier-Ethernet service as one virtual-connection instance (a MEF EVC).

entries.label: User-Network Interface (UNI)
entries.definition: The interface at which a subscriber site attaches to the carrier-Ethernet network.

entries.label: EVC endpoint
entries.definition: The endpoint of the EVC at one UNI.
entries.example: the EVC endpoint at the headquarters UNI

entries.label: customer broadcast segment
entries.definition: The customer VLAN carried by the service as a single layer-2 broadcast domain -- a forwarding domain, not a multi-homing link bundle.

entries.label: Bandwidth Profile
entries.definition: The committed/excess ingress rate policed at a UNI (a MEF bandwidth profile).

entries.label: Class of Service (CoS)
entries.definition: The forwarding-treatment class applied to service frames.
entries.example: the real-time class mapped from PCP 5

entries.label: source-MAC learning
entries.definition: Learning customer source-MAC addresses at a UNI to populate the forwarding table; distinct from handling a MAC that relocates.
entries.example: dynamic learning at the headquarters UNI

entries.label: service MTU
entries.definition: The maximum service frame size carried end to end.

entries.label: service availability objective
entries.definition: The service-level availability objective; a service-view construct with no network-model counterpart.
